rows.title: Email safety: redirect all non-production email to one inbox
rows.description: [18 Nov, founder] Previews/staging must never email the public. Add a redirect-all option to packages/payload-email-cloudflare: when set, every message's to/cc/bcc is replaced by one inbox, and the subject is prefixed '[<env> → original recipients]'. In apps/cms: redirect is ON unless the environment is explicitly production (ENVIRONMENT=production). The inbox comes from env EMAIL_REDIRECT_TO (set by the founder in Cloudflare; never in code). Previews get a send path (binding or Resend) so flows work, but always redirected. If redirect is required but EMAIL_REDIRECT_TO is missing, fall back to console, never deliver. Tests: production delivers normally, non-production always redirects, a missing inbox never delivers, cc/bcc stripped, original recipients shown.

rows.title: Cloudflare Access on the vwok site's preview + pre-launch hostnames

rows.title: Orders collection
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] SIMPLE + TRACEABLE credits. Jobs, orders and credits belong to the ORGANISATION (not the individual lister; createdBy is recorded for audit). No credit expiry in the MVP (hide PJ-21's per-plan creditExpiry field). Append-only ledger: every movement is one immutable row (bought +N via order, used −1 by job, refunded +1 when cancelled before publish, admin adjustment ±N with a required reason + who + when). Balance = sum of rows, never stored or editable. Organisation 'History' tab (admin + employer dashboard): one chronological list of orders, credit movements and job events (posted, published, expired, cancelled, relisted) with links, and a running-balance column plus a total row. Import (PJ-65) writes legacy packs as opening-balance ledger rows with legacy refs.

[19 Nov, founder] Member purchase permissions (set by the org owner, per member): 'use credits' default ON; 'buy (create invoiced order)' default OFF (owner always can). A member with no credits and no buy permission saves the job as 'Waiting for purchase'; the owner gets a one-click approve email that creates the order and invoice. Everything is shown in the org History tab with who did it. Configurable per tenant. FUTURE (post-MVP, with card payments): any member may pay by card (paid on the spot, no invoice liability) unless the owner disables it; logged in History.

rows.title: Job listing page + filters (SSR + edge cache)
rows.description:
[18 Nov, founder] No pagination on vwok in the MVP: show all live jobs with filters, lazy-loaded images. Add a guard: if a list exceeds ~200 items, enable Rocketship Pagination with `?page=N`. Expired jobs never appear in listings or search.

[19 Nov, founder] Filter URLs + SEO/GEO: clean indexable pages for one location and/or one category: /jobs/{category}, /jobs/{location}, /jobs/{location}/{category} (location first, NO '/in'). Category and location slugs must be unique per tenant ACROSS both collections (validation in PJ-16/17 + a test), so paths are unambiguous. A location page includes jobs in all descendant locations (tree), but URLs stay one level deep. Categories stay flat. Other filters (type, multiple values, salary, keyword) use query params: noindex, canonical to the nearest clean URL. Empty filtered page: 200 + 'No current X jobs in Y' + related links + alert sign-up, noindex while empty, left out of the sitemap, never a 404. GEO: server-rendered summary line ('12 IT jobs in Port Vila, updated today'), JobPosting on detail pages, ItemList JSON-LD on listings. Locations and categories are CMS-managed per tenant (seeded once from legacy). Configurable per tenant.

[19 Nov, founder] Search/filter behaviour: plain GET form (works without JS). If the selection is exactly one location and/or one category, 301 to the clean URL (/jobs/{location}/{category}); anything else stays on /jobs?... (noindex). Keyword search = ?q= using Postgres full-text search: no Elastic/Algolia (only ~100 live jobs). Server-rendered, cached full page loads; instant client-side updates can come later.

[19 Nov, founder] Filters = keyword, location, category, job type, salary band, date posted; each a per-tenant toggle (vwok = legacy). Clean URLs for category/location/type only; others are query params; no type+category/location path combos. /jobs/{type} for every type; per-type 'listed separately' flag hides those jobs from main listings/search (vwok: Volunteer on).

[19 Nov, founder] Junk URLs must never reach the CMS/DB: normalise the cache key before lookup. Unknown query params are dropped; known params (type, salary, posted, q, etc.) keep only values that exist (validated against the tenant's taxonomy/filter lists, themselves cached per content version); params are sorted. If normalisation changed the URL, 301 to the canonical URL (so /jobs?type=asdf123 -> /jobs, served from cache). Free-text keyword search is the only open input: rate-limited and cached per normalised query.

rows.title: Cache invalidation: CMS hooks purge site caches
rows.description:
[18 Nov, from PJ-35] launchpad's cached()/purgeTags use the Workers Cache API, which is per data centre, so purgeTags only clears the colo that runs it. PJ-41 needs a global purge: the Cloudflare zone purge-by-tag/URL API, or a shared version store (KV) the tags read from.

[19 Nov, founder] DECIDED cache strategy: per-tenant content version in Cloudflare KV, included in the edge cache key; CMS hooks bump it on any change to jobs, organisations, pages, menus, taxonomies, plans, site settings; the hourly expiry job bumps it when jobs expire/featured ends. TTLs: HTML at the edge 7 days; browser max-age 60s (browsers can't be purged); hashed assets 1 year immutable; images/R2 media 1 year. All public pages incl. directories (/jobs, category/location/type pages, organisations) cached this way. Nothing personal in cached HTML (signed-in UI and saved/viewed state client-side). Relative dates ('3 days ago') rendered client-side or as absolute dates. /health is never cached (checks Worker, CMS, DB); UptimeRobot monitors /health per site + CMS.

[19 Nov, founder] Signed-in state on cached pages: sign-in sets the HttpOnly session cookie plus a non-HttpOnly hint cookie (signed_in=1, no PII, same expiry as the session). Inline script swaps 'Sign in' for 'My account' from the hint (no request, no layout shift). Personal bits load from uncached /api/me; a 401 there clears the hint and reverts the header. /account and forms never cached; /account with an invalid session redirects to sign-in with a return URL. Sign-out clears both.

[19 Nov, founder] Junk URLs must never reach the CMS/DB: normalise the cache key before lookup. Unknown query params are dropped; known params (type, salary, posted, q, etc.) keep only values that exist (validated against the tenant's taxonomy/filter lists, themselves cached per content version); params are sorted. If normalisation changed the URL, 301 to the canonical URL (so /jobs?type=asdf123 -> /jobs, served from cache). Free-text keyword search is the only open input: rate-limited and cached per normalised query.

[19 Nov] Tracking params exception: utm_*, gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, li_fat_id, ref (list configurable) are IGNORED for the cache key but KEPT in the URL (never 301-stripped), so client-side analytics/Zaraz see them (e.g. ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com). Document in the README.

rows.title: Template renderer + `sendTemplate` + email log
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] All email is sent by the CMS (never the Astro site). One `sendTemplate(event, doc)` path does template lookup, the per-tenant on/off switch, the PJ-94 redirect and the log. One branded layout per tenant; templates supply only subject + body. Trim the legacy set to a short named event list (show it to the founder). Email log: NO bodies stored; event, template, tenant, linked record, status, time. Recipient address visible 90 days, then masked (j***@example.com); log rows deleted after 12 months; nightly job; both periods per tenant.

[19 Nov, founder] Package boundaries: payload-jobs must NOT hard-depend on @labcat2020/payload-email-liquid-templates. payload-jobs declares its email events + variable schemas and a sendEmail hook. If the Liquid plugin is installed (optional peerDependency), payload-jobs registers its default templates there (editable by site managers); otherwise simple built-in templates are used, or the app plugs in its own. Same rule for other cross-package links: optional peers + adapters.

[19 Nov, founder, FINAL] Email templates live INSIDE payload-jobs (no separate plugin, no Liquid). Per-tenant email templates: subject = plain text with an 'Insert variable' picker; body = Lexical rich text with an inline 'variable' chip node (First name, Job title, …), with variables declared per event. Per-tenant email settings: logo, colours, footer (Lexical). Send: Lexical → email-safe HTML (+ plain text), chips filled in (HTML-escaped), inside one tested responsive layout (Mailgun's open-source transactional template or MJML precompiled at build time). payload-jobs ships default texts per event. PJ-27's {{placeholder}} templates are migrated to the new format. Site managers never see code.

[19 Nov] Lists and loops (e.g. the alert digest's job list) are developer-built 'block chips' that site managers insert, e.g. 'Job list'. No template logic is exposed to editors.

rows.title: CI: site-key smoke on the preview
rows.description: In preview.yml, after Admin smoke: seed one tenant key and one aggregate key on the preview Neon branch, then call the cms REST API with x-site-key. Assert: tenant key sees only its tenant published docs; aggregate key sees published docs from all tenants; no key or a bad key is refused. Context: Kinsho asked for this on mission-control PR 12. Note: site keys are only sent server-side from Astro Workers, never from browsers.
rows.prompt:
# PJ-76: CI site-key smoke on the preview

## Repository and branch
Work in `LABCAT/mission-control`. Start from `main`, read the current code first, implement on a task branch and open a PR against `main`. Do not merge or deploy.

## Why
Kinsho asked for runtime evidence on mission-control PR 12. Site keys (`x-site-key` header, see `packages/payload-jobs/src/site-keys.ts`) let public Astro Workers read published content without a user session. Unit tests cover this (`apps/cms/src/tenancy.test.ts`), but nothing checks it against a real deployed preview.

## Change
In `.github/workflows/preview.yml`, add a job `site-key-smoke` (name: `Site-key smoke`) that runs after `publish`, alongside `admin-smoke`. It runs against that preview and its Neon branch:
1. **Seed** the preview's Neon branch (the connection string the `publish` job builds; expose it as a job output if it isn't already, and never echo it to logs):
   - two normal tenants (A, B) and the aggregate tenant
   - one **published** and one **draft** doc for A and for B, in a collection that has the site-key access override (find it in `apps/cms`)
   - three site keys: one on tenant A, one on the aggregate tenant, and a spare. Generate the raw keys in the job, store only their SHA-256 hex digest in `site_keys.key_hash` (same as `hashSiteKey`), and keep the raw keys in env only.

   Prefer a small TypeScript or Node script under `.github/scripts/` that uses Payload's local API, or plain SQL with `psql` if that's simpler. Make it idempotent (safe on re-runs).
2. **Call the preview's REST API** for that collection with `curl`, and assert:
   - tenant-A key → only tenant A's published doc (no B, no drafts)
   - aggregate key → published docs from A and B (no drafts)
   - no header → no tenant docs (check the status code or empty result)
   - a bad key (`sk_` + random) → refused or empty, same as no header
3. Fail the job with a clear message on any mismatch.

Don't change `mc-checks.yml`, `opencode-review.yml` or the deploy workflow. Don't use or print secrets beyond what preview.yml already uses.

## Tests
The job is the test. Push the branch and make sure `Site-key smoke` passes on this PR's preview. If you add a helper script, add a unit test for its pure parts (for example, the hashing matches `hashSiteKey`).

## Done when
- A PR exists that only touches `preview.yml` and any helper under `.github/scripts/`.
- `Site-key smoke` is green on the PR's own preview.
- **When you finish, mark this PR ready for review (not draft).**

rows.title: Lister/organisation dashboard on the Astro site (/account)
rows.description:
Astro SSR /account pages + Svelte islands (rocketship-svelte) for employers: organisation profile, my jobs (post, edit, end early, relist), checkout and orders, applicants per job + CSV. Svelte islands for interactive parts; prefetch + in-place updates for speed. /account is exempt from the zero-JS rule. This replaces the employer-facing parts of PJ-30/31/33/46; where site managers work is still open. Split into smaller tickets when dispatched.

[18 Nov, founder] The lister dashboard keeps the employer's own expired jobs (history, applicants, one-click relist); they aren't public.

[19 Nov, founder, PENDING final review; see docs/migration/PROPOSAL-ROLES.md] Organisation roles: owner (billing, profile, invite/remove members) + member (post/manage jobs, see applicants). Agency = its own organisation (type 'agency'); its jobs belong to it and optionally name a client (linked org, free text, or 'confidential'); client orgs can also post their own jobs. No separate site editor role for the MVP. Legacy recruiter users → members of an agency org. All configurable per tenant.

[19 Nov, founder] Never block a paying sign-up. A name match creates the organisation anyway, flagged 'possible duplicate'; the existing owner gets a one-click 'X wants to join' approve email (on approve the user and their jobs move into the existing org); otherwise a site manager merges the orgs (moving jobs, members, orders) or clears the flag. Needs a small 'merge organisations' admin tool.

[19 Nov, founder] Organisation pages are PRIVATE by default; the organisation owner chooses to make the page public. An org flagged 'possible duplicate' cannot be made public until the duplicate is resolved (owner-approved join, or a site manager merges or clears the flag). Jobs still show the organisation name either way. Imported vwok orgs that are public today: keep their current visibility (default), configurable per tenant.

[19 Nov, founder] An organisation page lists only the jobs of that (official) organisation. Jobs from a possible-duplicate organisation never appear on the official org's page until merged in (after the merge they move and show). The duplicate's jobs still appear in normal job listings under their own org name.

[19 Nov, founder] Job posting form: the job description uses Lexical (framework-agnostic core) in a small Svelte island with a minimal toolbar (headings, bold, italic, lists, links). It saves Lexical JSON, never HTML. The server validates against an allowlist of nodes and link protocols (http/https/mailto/tel). Legacy HTML is converted once at import (PJ-64) with the same allowlist. Multi-step flow kept (details → description → plan/checkout) with a progress indicator and drafts saved between steps. A reusable Lexical-Svelte editor is a candidate for rocketship-svelte (flag it in the PR).

[19 Nov, founder] SIMPLE + TRACEABLE credits. Jobs, orders and credits belong to the ORGANISATION (not the individual lister; createdBy is recorded for audit). No credit expiry in the MVP (hide PJ-21's per-plan creditExpiry field). Append-only ledger: every movement is one immutable row (bought +N via order, used −1 by job, refunded +1 when cancelled before publish, admin adjustment ±N with a required reason + who + when). Balance = sum of rows, never stored or editable. Organisation 'History' tab (admin + employer dashboard): one chronological list of orders, credit movements and job events (posted, published, expired, cancelled, relisted) with links, and a running-balance column plus a total row. Import (PJ-65) writes legacy packs as opening-balance ledger rows with legacy refs.

[19 Nov, founder] Member purchase permissions (set by the org owner, per member): 'use credits' default ON; 'buy (create invoiced order)' default OFF (owner always can). A member with no credits and no buy permission saves the job as 'Waiting for purchase'; the owner gets a one-click approve email that creates the order and invoice. Everything is shown in the org History tab with who did it. Configurable per tenant. FUTURE (post-MVP, with card payments): any member may pay by card (paid on the spot, no invoice liability) unless the owner disables it; logged in History.

[19 Nov, founder] Signed-in state on cached pages: sign-in sets the HttpOnly session cookie plus a non-HttpOnly hint cookie (signed_in=1, no PII, same expiry as the session). Inline script swaps 'Sign in' for 'My account' from the hint (no request, no layout shift). Personal bits load from uncached /api/me; a 401 there clears the hint and reverts the header. /account and forms never cached; /account with an invalid session redirects to sign-in with a return URL. Sign-out clears both.

rows.description:
Generic, npm-publishable package packages/rocketship-payload. Per-block subpath exports: /blocks/<name> (Payload block config), /astro/<name> (Astro component on @labcat2020/rocketship), /types. RenderBlocks takes an explicit component map so consumers only bundle the blocks they import. Blocks take plain data and never fetch; ship a small Payload Local API helper for in-process sites. The job sites keep fetching over REST with their site key. Start with hero, rich text (Lexical), card grid, CTA, FAQ. Inspiration: @payload-bites/astro-richtext-renderer, @orion-studios/payload-blocks, @grantcodes/astro-blocks.

[19 Nov, founder] The home page is BLOCK-BASED so site managers can rearrange it. Initial vwok home (imported in PJ-67) reproduces the legacy page: Hero (headline 'FIND A JOB IN VANUATU', tagline, job search form, 'Browse all jobs' link) → Feature boxes ×3 (icon, title, text, link; e.g. Search jobs, Employers) → Latest jobs (featured add-on jobs first, RSS link) → Rich text. Generic blocks (hero, feature boxes, rich text) come from rocketship-payload (PJ-84); job-specific blocks (search form, latest jobs) are registered by payload-jobs. Nothing new beyond the legacy content for the MVP.

rows.title: Production image variants via Cloudflare Images (1.x)
rows.description: 1.x, not MVP (founder, 18 Nov). Generate the media variants (320/640/960/1280, AVIF + WebP) in production with the Cloudflare Images binding (billed after a free allowance; confirm cost with the founder first). PJ-10 stores originals only in the Worker; variants are generated only under Node.

rows.title: rocketship-payload: contact form block (Payload form builder) + map block, Astro renderers
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Legacy vwok /contact has a contact form + a basic Google map. Rebuild as two generic blocks in rocketship-payload (PJ-84):
- Form block: use the official Payload form builder plugin (@payloadcms/plugin-form-builder; check Payload 4 beta support). Submissions emailed through our CMS email path (PJ-92/PJ-50), Turnstile on submit, per-tenant forms. Astro renderer: use an existing Astro package for the form builder if a maintained one exists; otherwise build it inside rocketship-payload (per-block export, generic, Local API based).
- Map block: no-API-key embed (Google Maps embed URL or OpenStreetMap iframe), lazy-loaded.
- Import: recreate vwok's contact page with these two blocks.

[19 Nov, founder] Renderer is plain Astro (HTML form, no Svelte), living in rocketship-payload and using Rocketship form components for inputs. Add a Payload queue job that deletes form submissions older than a per-tenant site setting (form submission retention, days; default 90; 0 = do not store, email only). PII must not outlive the setting.

rows.title: System pages: seeded per site, undeletable, role rules
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Pages collection gets a 'role' field: home, about, contact, organisations (null = normal page).
- Seeded when a site/tenant is created. Cannot be deleted (unpublish only). Role cannot be changed/removed by site managers.
- home: served at /, no slug, no parent, no children (top-level pages are its siblings).
- organisations: no children (/organisations/{slug} is reserved for organisation pages); contains the Organisation directory block plus any other blocks (e.g. promo tile).
- about/contact: normal pages, may have children; contact seeded with form + map blocks (PJ-102).
- No home/organisations pickers in site settings; role marks the page.

rows.title: Application retention: delete applications + CV files 12 months after the job closes
rows.description: [18 Nov, founder] Applications (PJ-25) and their CV/cover-letter files stay in the employer dashboard for 12 months after the job closes, with CSV export and downloads; then a daily job (PJ-08 runner, overrideAccess) deletes the records and their R2 files. Retention period configurable per tenant (default 12 months). An admin action deletes an applicant's data on request. Tests: boundary dates, files removed from R2, tenant isolation.

rows.title: GEO: structured data + agent-friendly site (llms.txt, AI crawler setting)
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] One SEO tab (no separate GEO tab). Structured data is generated automatically from content, no manual fields: JobPosting (live jobs only), Organization (site + organisation pages), WebSite + SearchAction, BreadcrumbList, AboutPage/ContactPage, ItemList on listing pages.
- /llms.txt generated per tenant (site summary + key URLs).
- Per-tenant setting: allow AI crawlers in robots.txt (default allow).
- Semantic HTML; validate with Google Rich Results test in e2e/CI where feasible.

rows.title: Privacy policy + terms: footer links and consent lines on forms
rows.description: [18 Nov, founder] The new vwok site needs a privacy policy (the legacy site may not have one; check the live site). Agent part: the privacy and terms pages as CMS pages (PJ-20/39), footer links, and a consent line linking to the policy on the apply, alert and registration forms. The policy text (data use, 12-month application retention, deletion requests) is written or approved by the FOUNDER.

rows.title: Generated share images (OG) for jobs, organisations, home
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Auto-generated share (Open Graph) images, 1200x630 PNG (not AVIF: social scrapers don't reliably support it).
- Worker route e.g. /og/jobs/{id}.png; template: job title, organisation logo (fallback: site logo), location, job type, tenant colours/logo from site settings.
- Generated on first request, stored in R2, edge-cached; regenerated/invalidated when the job changes.
- Same for organisation pages and the home page.
- Optimised PNG (~60-100 KB). Satori + resvg-wasm or equivalent that runs on Workers.

rows.title: IDEA (post-MVP): Stripe add-on + collect-on-behalf payouts via Wise
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] IDEA (post-MVP, needs accountant/legal first): collect card payments on behalf of tenants that can't get Stripe themselves (e.g. Vanuatu).
Flow: LABCAT NZ Stripe account charges in tenant currency (VUV supported, zero-decimal) -> settles NZD -> scheduled payout via Wise Business API (NZ accounts can fund transfers via API; VUV payouts exist, API support for VUV to confirm with Wise) to the tenant's local bank account. Per-tenant payout ledger + statements.
Concerns: LABCAT becomes merchant of record / payment facilitator (tax, AML, refunds, chargebacks); double FX + fees (~3-5%).
Core needs only the generic 'payment provider' plug point; Stripe = add-on package.

rows.title: Email deliverability: bounce/complaint events, suppression, email log status
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Track deliverability with Cloudflare Email Service delivery events (message.delivered/deferred/bounced/failed/rejected/complained) via the per-domain event subscription -> Cloudflare Queue -> consumer in the CMS worker.
- Update the email log status per message (match payload.messageId to the send binding id; check angle-bracket format).
- Hard bounce / complaint: suppress the address for that tenant; pause its alerts and show 'email bouncing' to admins/the user. Soft bounces: record only.
- Admin: email log filters by status; simple deliverability numbers (sent/delivered/bounced/complaints, last 30 days).
- Verify current Cloudflare docs for the event schema before building. Note: Email Service is transactional-only; alerts are opt-in notifications, keep them minimal and with List-Unsubscribe.

rows.title: Slugs unique across job categories and locations per tenant
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] For clean filter URLs without '/in': enforce that a category slug never equals a location slug (or a reserved word like 'page') within one tenant, both ways, with a clear admin error. Tests. Small; packages/payload-jobs. No migration expected unless an index is needed.

[19 Nov, founder] Job type slugs are included: unique across categories, locations and job types.

rows.title: IDEA (maybe never): seeker profiles (private apply profile / hub professional page)
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] IDEA only (very low priority, maybe never). No seeker profiles in the MVP.
Possible futures: (a) private profile: saved CV/details that prefill the apply form, shared only with employers you apply to; (b) for a pacificjobs.com hub: an opt-in professional 'who I am' page (LinkedIn-style, not 'looking for work'). Concerns: small-island privacy, stale/spam profiles, PII risk, unproven demand (legacy resumes unused).

rows.title: Generic location tree: drop fixed island/town kinds; per-tenant level labels
rows.description: [19 Nov, founder] Locations must be generic, not Vanuatu-specific. Replace PJ-17's fixed `kind` enum (region|island|town) with a plain parent/child tree (depth computed, optional max depth per tenant). Tenant settings define level labels (e.g. vwok: ['Island','Town']; another site: ['Region','City']) used in the admin and on public filters. Keep the 'parent must be same tenant, no cycles' rules. Migration: map existing kinds to depth, drop the enum; vwok seed gets labels ['Island','Town'] (legacy picker shape). Tests: arbitrary depth, labels per tenant, tenant isolation, no cycles. Works with PJ-98 (unique slugs).

rows.title: Email sign-in (magic link + code), 90-day sessions, passwords optional
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Sign-in for the MVP: (1) email sign-in: one email with BOTH a magic link and a 6-digit code (link on same device, code on another); resend after 30s; 'check your spam folder' hint; codes expire in 15 min, single use, rate-limited. (2) Passwords kept as an option (Payload built-in; legacy WP hashes via PJ-34). (3) Sessions last 90 days. Google/Microsoft login post-MVP (decide with query 17). No Facebook login.

[19 Nov, founder] Signed-in state on cached pages: sign-in sets the HttpOnly session cookie plus a non-HttpOnly hint cookie (signed_in=1, no PII, same expiry as the session). Inline script swaps 'Sign in' for 'My account' from the hint (no request, no layout shift). Personal bits load from uncached /api/me; a 401 there clears the hint and reverts the header. /account and forms never cached; /account with an invalid session redirects to sign-in with a return URL. Sign-out clears both.

[19 Nov, founder] REPLACES the 90-day session: 'Keep me signed in' checkbox. Unticked: session ends after 1 day. Ticked: 30 days, rolling (renewed on use). Both durations per-tenant settings (vwok 1 / 30). Hint cookie matches the session expiry.

rows.title: Analytics in the admin + per-job stats for employers
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Analytics inside the product (no Cloudflare dashboard access for tenants).
- Site managers (Payload admin dashboard widget, per tenant): visitors/page views (last 7/30 days), top pages, top referrers – pulled from the Cloudflare Web Analytics GraphQL API (server-side, cached ~1h; API token is a secret in env) – plus our own numbers: job views, applications, new alert subscribers, orders.
- Employers (/account): views and applications per job (legacy showed job stats to listers: jr_ad_stats_all = 1).
- Job view counting already planned (PJ-38/PJ-53); legacy totals imported.

[19 Nov, founder] Split: (1) traffic panel = generic Payload plugin packages/payload-cloudflare-analytics (@labcat2020/payload-cloudflare-analytics), not job-specific, multi-tenant aware (site tag per tenant), like payload-email-cloudflare. (2) Job stats (views/applications per job, admin numbers) = payload-jobs core.

rows.title: Viewed jobs label + recently viewed (localStorage)
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] 'Viewed' jobs, browser-only (localStorage, wrapped in try/catch; no server, no PII, works signed out).
- Job detail page records the job id (keep last 20).
- Job cards show a 'Viewed' label; a 'Recently viewed' list (last 5-10) on the jobs page and in /account.
- Must not affect the 100 PageSpeed score: tiny inline script, run after load/idle, no layout shift (reserve space or apply label without moving content), no framework hydration just for this.
- No import of legacy _viewed_jobs.

rows.title: payload-email-smtp: SMTP transport package for Workers
rows.description: [19 Nov, founder] Generic SMTP email transport for Workers (no server): new package packages/payload-email-smtp. Per-tenant transport setting (Cloudflare default, or tenant SMTP); vwok uses YCV Google Workspace SMTP. Bounce tracking only on Cloudflare.

rows.title: Site manager how-to inside the admin
rows.description: [19 Nov, founder] Short how-to for site managers inside the Payload admin (a 'Help' page/dashboard link), per tenant-neutral wording: posting a job for an org, approving jobs/org pages, orders + invoices (Xero), credits, coupons, pages/blocks/menus, alerts, reports, analytics panel, privacy/deletion requests. Written from the finished screens just before launch, with screenshots. No videos/sessions unless YCV asks.

rows.title: payload-backups: off-site DB + media backups plugin (post-MVP)
rows.description:
[19 Nov, founder] Post-MVP. UpdraftPlus-style backups as a GENERIC Payload plugin (not job-specific): @labcat2020/payload-backups.
- Scheduled (Payload jobs/cron): daily database export (Payload Local API -> NDJSON per collection, gzipped; Workers can't run pg_dump) + media sync (new/changed R2 objects) to an off-site, S3-compatible destination on a different provider/account (e.g. Backblaze B2) or Google Drive.
- Retention: e.g. 7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly. Admin page: last backup status, sizes, download link, 'back up now'; alert on failure.
- Restore: documented CLI/admin restore into an empty database + media bucket; test restore regularly.
- Must survive deleting the R2 bucket or the Neon project (different provider/credentials). No secrets logged.
MVP covers: Neon 7-day restore + one-off UpdraftPlus archive of the old site to Google Drive at decommission (PJ-75). Also enable R2 bucket protections where available (bucket lock/retention) for the media bucket.

rows.title: Tenant deletion: super-admin only, block while data exists, offboarding clean-up (post-MVP, design first)
rows.description: [18 Nov, founder] POST-MVP, low priority: needs a design discussion with the founder before dispatch. Problem (found in PJ-21): deleting a tenant leaves its documents orphaned (tenant FK is ON DELETE SET NULL, so the multi-tenant plugin's afterDelete clean-up matches nothing). Agreed so far: only super-admins can delete a tenant; block the delete while the tenant still has data. To design later: a tenant clean-up/offboarding script that removes the tenant's job-board data (jobs, organisations, plans, orders, applications, taxonomies, media/R2 files, email templates, settings) while user ACCOUNTS survive (only that tenant's memberships are removed). Export first (data ownership/exit terms, PLAN.md open question), dry-run mode, audit log.

rows.title: AI job search (post-MVP)
rows.description: [19 Nov, founder] POST-MVP, founder is keen. Natural-language / semantic job search ('describe the job you want') for small sites, staying on Cloudflare: Workers AI embeddings + Vectorize index per tenant, updated by job hooks; fall back to keyword search. Possible extras: 'jobs like this', alert matching. Needs a design + cost check with the founder before dispatch.
